## Quality Check of the data

### Analysis setup

This document performs the quality control of the glioblastoma sample dissociated with the gentleMACS Octo Dissociator. The sample originates from the same donor and FFPE specimen as the manually dissociated sample, and was processed with the same probe panel, in the same GEM lane and with the same Cell Ranger version (7.1.0). The dissociation method is therefore the only experimental difference between the two samples.

The workflow, including the ambient RNA correction with `SoupX`, and the thresholds are identical to those applied to the Manual sample, so that the quality metrics of both samples are directly comparable. A fixed random seed was used to ensure reproducibility; it was reset before each stochastic step (rounding of the corrected counts and doublet detection).

```{r}
# Define the sample information
sample.name <- "brain_octo"
sample_label <- "Octo"
species <- "Human"

# Set a fixed random seed for reproducibility
the.seed <- 42
set.seed(the.seed)

# Load the packages required for quality control and doublet detection
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(scDblFinder)
  library(SoupX)
})
```

The quality-control thresholds were defined once and are identical to those of the Manual sample. The number of cells called by Cell Ranger for each sample, as reported on the 10x Genomics dataset page, was recorded as an external reference.

```{r}
# Define the QC thresholds, identical to those of the Manual sample
minGenes <- 800
minUmi <- 1000
maxpct_mt <- 10

# Cells called by Cell Ranger for each sample (10x Genomics dataset page)
cellranger_cells <- c(Manual = 4620, Octo = 4599)

# Format numbers consistently in the text
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
```

Dataset from 10x Genomics: Mixture of Lung Cancer and Glioblastoma FFPE Tissues Dissociated Manually or using gentleMACS Dissociator, Multiplexed Samples, 4 Probe Barcodes (Next GEM). Sample used: Brain Cancer, Octo Dissociator.

<https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/mixture-of-lung-cancer-and-glioblastoma-ffpe-tissues-dissociated-manually-or-using-gentlemacs-dissociator-multiplexed-samples-4-probe-barcodes-1-standard>

## Loading the raw count matrix

The raw feature-barcode matrix of the Octo-dissociated glioblastoma sample was used, as for the Manual sample. It contains both cell-containing droplets and a large number of empty droplets.

```{r}
# Define the path to the raw 10x Genomics feature-barcode matrix
raw_data_path <- "../data/raw_data/sample_raw_feature_bc_matrix_octo"
stopifnot(dir.exists(raw_data_path))

# Read the sparse count matrix
scmat <- Read10X(
  data.dir = raw_data_path
)

# Keep the gene-expression matrix if several feature types were returned
if (is.list(scmat)) scmat <- scmat[["Gene Expression"]]

# Verify the structure of the imported object
class(scmat)
dim(scmat)
```

The dimensions of the raw matrix were recorded before filtering.

```{r}
# Record the dimensions of the unfiltered matrix
n_raw_features <- nrow(scmat)
n_raw_barcodes <- ncol(scmat)

cat("Raw features:", n_raw_features, "\n")
cat("Raw barcodes:", n_raw_barcodes, "\n")
```

The raw matrix contained `r fmt(n_raw_features)` features and `r fmt(n_raw_barcodes)` barcodes. At this stage, barcodes should not all be interpreted as cells because the raw matrix includes empty droplets and background RNA.

## Barcode-rank curve

The total number of UMIs was calculated for every barcode. Barcodes were then ranked from the highest to the lowest RNA content to generate a barcode-rank, or knee, plot.

```{r}
# Calculate the total number of UMIs detected in each barcode
nb_umi_by_barcode <- data.frame(
  barcode = colnames(scmat),
  nb_umi = Matrix::colSums(scmat)
)

# Rank barcodes from the highest to the lowest UMI count
nb_umi_by_barcode <- nb_umi_by_barcode %>%
  arrange(desc(nb_umi)) %>%
  mutate(barcode_rank = seq_len(n()))

# Count the barcodes above the applied UMI threshold and above the Manual knee
n_above_minumi <- sum(nb_umi_by_barcode$nb_umi > minUmi)
n_above_knee <- sum(nb_umi_by_barcode$nb_umi > 3000)
```

The curve was used as a diagnostic representation of the transition between RNA-rich droplets and the background population. The applied UMI threshold and the knee position identified visually for the Manual sample (3,000 UMIs) are shown as dashed lines.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

# Plot the barcode-rank curve with the reference thresholds
nb_umi_by_barcode %>%
  filter(nb_umi > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = barcode_rank, y = nb_umi)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = minUmi, colour = "green", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3000, colour = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10(name = "Droplet rank (log scale)") +
  scale_y_log10(name = "Number of UMIs per droplet (log scale)") +
  labs(title = paste0("Barcode-rank plot of the ", sample.name, " sample")) +
  theme_classic()
```

A total of `r fmt(n_above_minumi)` barcodes exceeded the applied threshold of `r fmt(minUmi)` UMIs and `r fmt(n_above_knee)` barcodes exceeded 3,000 UMIs, compared with `r fmt(cellranger_cells[["Octo"]])` cells called by Cell Ranger for this sample.

The transition was not used as a strict automated cell-calling threshold: subsequent filtering was based on the observed gene, UMI and mitochondrial distributions. As the raw matrix was used, the initial gene and UMI filters also acted as an empirical empty-droplet filter. A statistical method such as `DropletUtils::emptyDrops()` could be used as a complementary sensitivity analysis, but it was not used to define the primary dataset in this workflow.

## Ambient RNA correction

Barcodes containing RNA released by lysed cells can carry a background signal that is shared across all droplets. This ambient RNA was estimated and removed with `SoupX`, using the empty droplets of the raw matrix to define the background profile and the candidate cells (barcodes with at least 200 detected genes) as the cell-containing droplets.

```{r}
# Define the candidate cells (barcodes with at least 200 detected genes)
cell_barcodes <- colnames(scmat)[Matrix::colSums(scmat > 0) >= 200]
filt_mat <- scmat[, cell_barcodes]

# Initialise the SoupChannel with the raw and the candidate-cell matrices
sc <- SoupChannel(tod = scmat, toc = filt_mat)
```

SoupX requires a partition of the cells to identify cell-type-specific markers. A temporary clustering of the candidate cells was therefore performed; it was used only for the estimation of the contamination fraction.

```{r}
# Perform a temporary clustering of the candidate cells
sobj_temp <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = filt_mat)
sobj_temp <- NormalizeData(sobj_temp, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_temp <- FindVariableFeatures(sobj_temp, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_temp <- ScaleData(sobj_temp, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_temp <- RunPCA(sobj_temp, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_temp <- FindNeighbors(sobj_temp, dims = 1:20, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_temp <- FindClusters(sobj_temp, resolution = 0.5, verbose = FALSE)

# Provide the clusters to SoupX
sc <- setClusters(sc, setNames(sobj_temp$seurat_clusters, colnames(sobj_temp)))
```

The global contamination fraction (rho) was estimated automatically, with the default SoupX parameters written explicitly.

```{r}
# Estimate the ambient RNA contamination fraction
sc <- autoEstCont(sc, tfidfMin = 1.0, soupQuantile = 0.90,
                  priorRho = 0.05, priorRhoStdDev = 0.1)

# Record the estimated contamination fraction
soupx_rho <- sc$fit$rhoEst
```

The corrected counts were generated as integers for downstream compatibility. Rounding to integers is stochastic, so the seed was reset immediately before this step.

```{r}
# Reset the seed before the stochastic rounding of the corrected counts
set.seed(the.seed)

# Generate the corrected count matrix
adj_matrix <- adjustCounts(sc, roundToInt = TRUE)
```

The overall impact of the correction was assessed from the amount of RNA removed and from the genes forming the main part of the background.

```{r}
# Quantify the ambient UMIs removed from the candidate cells
removed_counts <- filt_mat - adj_matrix
total_original <- sum(filt_mat)
total_removed <- sum(removed_counts)
soupx_pct_removed <- round(100 * total_removed / total_original, 2)

# Identify the genes most affected by the correction
top_soup_genes <- head(sort(Matrix::rowSums(removed_counts), decreasing = TRUE), 10)

cat("Estimated contamination fraction (rho):", round(soupx_rho, 3), "\n")
cat("Ambient UMIs removed:", total_removed, "(", soupx_pct_removed, "% of the UMIs of the candidate cells )\n")
print(top_soup_genes)
```

The estimated contamination fraction was `r round(soupx_rho, 3)`, and `r soupx_pct_removed`% of the UMIs of the candidate cells were removed. The genes most affected were `r paste(names(top_soup_genes), collapse = ", ")`.

## Initial creation of the Seurat object

An initial Seurat object was created from the corrected counts by retaining genes detected in at least five barcodes and barcodes containing at least 200 detected genes. This first permissive filtering step removed the lowest-complexity portion of the matrix while preserving candidate cells for further inspection.

```{r}
# Create an initial Seurat object using permissive thresholds
sobj <- CreateSeuratObject(
  counts = adj_matrix,
  min.cells = 5,
  min.features = 200,
  project = sample.name
)

# Record the dimensions after the initial Seurat filtering
n_initial_cells <- ncol(sobj)
n_retained_genes <- nrow(sobj)

cat("Candidate barcodes:", n_initial_cells, "\n")
cat("Retained genes:", n_retained_genes, "\n")
```

The initial object contained `r fmt(n_initial_cells)` candidate barcodes and `r fmt(n_retained_genes)` genes.

The percentage of mitochondrial transcripts was calculated for every candidate barcode from the genes beginning with `MT-`. Its distribution was assessed after the complexity filtering, in the dedicated section below.

```{r}
# Calculate the percentage of mitochondrial transcripts in each barcode
sobj$percent_mt <- PercentageFeatureSet(sobj, pattern = "^MT-")

# Inspect the metadata generated by Seurat
head(sobj@meta.data)

# Inspect a small portion of the count matrix using the public accessor
GetAssayData(sobj, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")[1:5, 1:5]
```

The raw and intermediate matrices were no longer required after creation of the Seurat object.

```{r}
# Remove large intermediate objects to release memory
rm(nb_umi_by_barcode, scmat, filt_mat, adj_matrix, removed_counts, sobj_temp, sc)
gc()
```

## Gene complexity assessment

The number of detected genes per barcode was used to identify droplets with insufficient transcriptional complexity. Low-complexity barcodes may represent empty droplets, cell debris or severely damaged cells.

```{r}
# Summarise the number of genes detected per candidate barcode
summary(sobj$nFeature_RNA)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5

# Visualise the distribution of detected genes
p_genes_hist <- ggplot(sobj@meta.data, aes(x = nFeature_RNA)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 200, fill = "grey70", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = minGenes, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Detected genes per barcode", x = "Number of detected genes",
       y = "Number of barcodes") +
  theme_classic()

p_genes_vln <- VlnPlot(sobj, features = "nFeature_RNA", pt.size = 0.01) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = minGenes, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  NoLegend()

p_genes_hist + p_genes_vln
```

The distribution contained a large population of low-complexity barcodes, with a median of `r fmt(median(sobj$nFeature_RNA))` detected genes among the candidate barcodes. The minimum threshold of `r fmt(minGenes)` detected genes, applied to the Manual sample, was retained.

No upper gene-count threshold was applied at this stage. Brain and tumour cells can exhibit high transcriptional complexity, and an arbitrary upper cut-off could remove genuine biological populations. Potential multiplets were evaluated later using `scDblFinder`.

## UMI-count assessment

The total UMI count per barcode provides an additional measure of RNA content. Barcodes with very low UMI counts are less likely to contain intact, transcriptionally informative cells.

```{r}
# Summarise the total number of UMIs per candidate barcode
summary(sobj$nCount_RNA)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5

# Visualise the UMI-count distribution on linear and logarithmic scales
p_umi_lin <- VlnPlot(sobj, features = "nCount_RNA", pt.size = 0.01) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = minUmi, colour = "green", linetype = "dashed") +
  NoLegend()

p_umi_log <- VlnPlot(sobj, features = "nCount_RNA", log = TRUE, pt.size = 0.01) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = minUmi, colour = "green", linetype = "dashed") +
  NoLegend()

p_umi_lin + p_umi_log
```

The relationship between the number of detected genes and the total UMI count was examined to identify the main complexity trend and potential extreme observations.

```{r}
# Calculate the correlation between gene and UMI counts
gene_umi_correlation <- cor(sobj$nFeature_RNA, sobj$nCount_RNA, method = "pearson")
gene_umi_correlation
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6

# Visualise the gene-UMI relationship
FeatureScatter(sobj, feature1 = "nCount_RNA", feature2 = "nFeature_RNA", pt.size = 0.1) +
  labs(title = paste0("Gene-UMI relationship (Pearson r = ",
                      round(gene_umi_correlation, 2), ")"))
```

The two metrics were positively correlated (Pearson r = `r round(gene_umi_correlation, 2)`), as expected for droplets containing increasing amounts of cellular RNA. The minimum threshold of `r fmt(minUmi)` UMIs, applied to the Manual sample, was retained.

## Filtering low-complexity barcodes

Barcodes were retained when they contained more than `r fmt(minGenes)` detected genes and more than `r fmt(minUmi)` UMIs.

```{r}
# Retain barcodes satisfying both complexity criteria
sobjFiltrd <- subset(sobj, subset = nFeature_RNA > minGenes & nCount_RNA > minUmi)

# Record the number of candidate cells after gene and UMI filtering
n_after_complexity <- ncol(sobjFiltrd)

cat("Cells after gene and UMI filtering:", n_after_complexity, "\n")
```

The joint gene and UMI filtering retained `r fmt(n_after_complexity)` candidate cells.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5

# Inspect the distributions after complexity filtering
VlnPlot(sobjFiltrd, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA"), ncol = 2, pt.size = 0.01)

FeatureScatter(sobjFiltrd, feature1 = "nCount_RNA", feature2 = "nFeature_RNA", pt.size = 0.1)
```

The metadata of the candidate barcodes was kept for the threshold-sensitivity analysis, and the unfiltered Seurat object was removed.

```{r}
# Keep the candidate-level metrics for the sensitivity analysis
candidate_meta <- sobj@meta.data[, c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent_mt")]

# Remove the initial object to reduce memory usage
rm(sobj)
gc()
```

## Mitochondrial transcript assessment

An increased mitochondrial proportion can indicate damaged or dying cells, although the expected distribution depends on the tissue-processing and sequencing protocol.

```{r}
# Summarise the mitochondrial percentage
summary(sobjFiltrd$percent_mt)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 5

# Visualise the mitochondrial-percentage distribution
p_mt_vln <- VlnPlot(sobjFiltrd, features = "percent_mt", pt.size = 0.01) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = maxpct_mt, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  NoLegend()

p_mt_hist <- ggplot(sobjFiltrd@meta.data, aes(x = percent_mt)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100, colour = "black", fill = "grey70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = maxpct_mt, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Mitochondrial transcript percentage",
       x = "Mitochondrial transcripts (%)", y = "Number of cells") +
  theme_classic()

p_mt_vln + p_mt_hist
```

The relationship between mitochondrial percentage and total UMI count was examined to assess whether mitochondria-enriched cells also tended to have reduced RNA content.

```{r}
# Calculate the correlation between mitochondrial percentage and UMI count
mito_umi_correlation <- cor(sobjFiltrd$percent_mt, sobjFiltrd$nCount_RNA, method = "pearson")
mito_umi_correlation
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4

# Visualise the mitochondrial content against the UMI count
FeatureScatter(sobjFiltrd, feature1 = "nCount_RNA", feature2 = "percent_mt", pt.size = 0.1) +
  labs(title = paste0("Mitochondrial content and UMI count (Pearson r = ",
                      round(mito_umi_correlation, 2), ")"))
```

A total of `r round(100 * mean(sobjFiltrd$percent_mt < maxpct_mt), 1)`% of the candidate cells had a mitochondrial percentage below the `r maxpct_mt`% threshold applied to the Manual sample, which is appropriate for the FFPE probe-based nature of the dataset. The correlation between mitochondrial percentage and UMI count was `r round(mito_umi_correlation, 2)`.

```{r}
# Remove cells with elevated mitochondrial transcript proportions
sobjFiltrd <- subset(sobjFiltrd, subset = percent_mt < maxpct_mt)

# Record the number of cells after mitochondrial filtering
n_after_mito <- ncol(sobjFiltrd)
n_removed_mito <- n_after_complexity - n_after_mito

cat("Cells after mitochondrial filtering:", n_after_mito, "\n")
cat("Cells removed by mitochondrial filtering:", n_removed_mito, "\n")
```

The mitochondrial filter retained `r fmt(n_after_mito)` cells and removed `r fmt(n_removed_mito)` cells.

## Threshold sensitivity

The impact of the three thresholds on the number of retained cells was quantified on the candidate barcodes. The grid below varies the gene and UMI thresholds around the applied values; 3,000 UMIs corresponds to the knee position of the Manual sample. The mitochondrial threshold was kept at `r maxpct_mt`%.

```{r}
# Build the grid of alternative gene and UMI thresholds
threshold_grid <- expand.grid(min_genes = c(600, 800, 1000),
                              min_umi = c(1000, 2000, 3000))

# Count the cells retained under each combination of thresholds
threshold_grid$cells_retained <- mapply(
  function(g, u) sum(candidate_meta$nFeature_RNA > g &
                       candidate_meta$nCount_RNA > u &
                       candidate_meta$percent_mt < maxpct_mt),
  threshold_grid$min_genes, threshold_grid$min_umi
)

# Flag the combination applied in this workflow
threshold_grid$applied <- threshold_grid$min_genes == minGenes &
  threshold_grid$min_umi == minUmi

threshold_grid
```

Across the grid, the number of retained cells ranged from `r fmt(min(threshold_grid$cells_retained))` to `r fmt(max(threshold_grid$cells_retained))`; the applied thresholds retained `r fmt(threshold_grid$cells_retained[threshold_grid$applied])` cells before doublet removal.

## Doublet detection

Droplets containing two or more cells can generate hybrid transcriptional profiles and artificial connections between otherwise distinct populations. Doublets were identified using `scDblFinder`, applied to this sample alone.

The Seurat object was temporarily converted into a `SingleCellExperiment`, which is the input format expected by `scDblFinder`.

```{r}
# Convert the Seurat object into a SingleCellExperiment
sceobj <- as.SingleCellExperiment(sobjFiltrd)

# Reset the seed before the stochastic doublet-detection step
set.seed(the.seed)

# Detect putative doublets
doublet_res <- scDblFinder(sceobj)
```

The predicted doublet classifications and scores were transferred back to the Seurat metadata.

```{r}
# Store the doublet classifications and scores in the Seurat object
sobjFiltrd$doublets.class <- doublet_res$scDblFinder.class
sobjFiltrd$doublets.score <- doublet_res$scDblFinder.score

# Display the number and proportion of predicted singlets and doublets
doublet_table <- table(sobjFiltrd$doublets.class)
doublet_proportions <- round(100 * prop.table(doublet_table), 1)

doublet_table
doublet_proportions
```

```{r}
# Record the number of predicted doublets
n_doublets <- sum(sobjFiltrd$doublets.class == "doublet")
doublet_percentage <- round(100 * n_doublets / ncol(sobjFiltrd), 1)

cat("Predicted doublets:", n_doublets, "\n")
cat("Predicted doublet percentage:", doublet_percentage, "%\n")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

# Visualise the doublet-score distribution by predicted class
ggplot(sobjFiltrd@meta.data, aes(x = doublets.score, fill = doublets.class)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "scDblFinder score by predicted class", x = "Doublet score",
       y = "Number of cells", fill = "Class") +
  theme_classic()
```

`r fmt(n_doublets)` cells (`r doublet_percentage`%) were predicted to be doublets. Predicted doublets were removed before dimensionality reduction and clustering.

```{r}
# Retain only cells classified as singlets
sobjFiltrd <- subset(sobjFiltrd, subset = doublets.class == "singlet")

# Record the final number of retained cells
n_final_cells <- ncol(sobjFiltrd)

cat("Final number of singlets:", n_final_cells, "\n")
```

The intermediate `SingleCellExperiment` objects were removed after doublet detection.

```{r}
# Remove intermediate doublet-detection objects
rm(sceobj, doublet_res)
gc()
```

## Final quality-control assessment

The final distributions of detected genes, UMI counts and mitochondrial percentage were inspected after all filtering steps.

```{r}
# Display summary statistics for the final dataset
summary(sobjFiltrd$nFeature_RNA)
summary(sobjFiltrd$nCount_RNA)
summary(sobjFiltrd$percent_mt)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 5

# Visualise the final QC distributions
VlnPlot(sobjFiltrd, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent_mt"), ncol = 3,
        pt.size = 0.01)
```

A summary table documents the number of barcodes or cells retained at each step of the workflow.

```{r}
# Summarise the number of barcodes or cells retained after each QC step
qc_summary <- data.frame(
  step = c("Raw barcodes", "Initial Seurat filtering", "Gene and UMI filtering",
           "Mitochondrial filtering", "Doublet removal"),
  retained_barcodes_or_cells = c(n_raw_barcodes, n_initial_cells, n_after_complexity,
                                 n_after_mito, n_final_cells)
)

qc_summary
```

The final dataset contained `r fmt(n_final_cells)` predicted singlets and `r fmt(n_retained_genes)` retained genes. These cells passed the gene-complexity, UMI-count and mitochondrial-content filters and were not classified as doublets.

## QC comparison with the Manual sample

The Manual sample was processed with the same workflow, ambient RNA correction and thresholds. Its filtered object was loaded in a separate environment, so that the Octo object is not overwritten, and only its cell-level metadata was retained.

```{r}
# Locate the filtered object of the Manual sample (file-name case is ignored)
manual_file <- list.files("../data/processed_data",
                          pattern = "^brain_DV200_FILTERED\\.rda$",
                          ignore.case = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(manual_file) == 1)

# Load the object in a separate environment and keep the cell-level metadata
manual_env <- new.env()
load(manual_file, envir = manual_env)
manual_meta <- manual_env$sobjFiltrd@meta.data

# Verify that the QC metrics are available
metric_cols <- c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent_mt")
stopifnot(all(metric_cols %in% colnames(manual_meta)))

# Retrieve the QC summary stored with the Manual object (NULL if absent)
get_misc <- function(obj, slot) tryCatch(Misc(obj, slot = slot), error = function(e) NULL)
manual_funnel <- get_misc(manual_env$sobjFiltrd, "qc_funnel")
manual_soupx <- get_misc(manual_env$sobjFiltrd, "soupx")

# Release the memory used by the Manual object
n_manual_final <- nrow(manual_meta)
rm(manual_env)
gc()
```

The cell-level QC metrics of both samples were combined into a single table.

```{r}
# Combine the QC metrics of the two samples
qc_metrics <- bind_rows(
  Manual = manual_meta[, metric_cols],
  Octo = sobjFiltrd@meta.data[, metric_cols],
  .id = "sample"
)
qc_metrics$sample <- factor(qc_metrics$sample, levels = c("Manual", "Octo"))

# Summarise the QC metrics by sample
qc_summary_by_sample <- qc_metrics %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(cells = n(),
            median_genes = median(nFeature_RNA), IQR_genes = IQR(nFeature_RNA),
            median_umi = median(nCount_RNA), IQR_umi = IQR(nCount_RNA),
            median_pct_mt = round(median(percent_mt), 2),
            IQR_pct_mt = round(IQR(percent_mt), 2))

qc_summary_by_sample
```

The distributions were compared with the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic D, used as an effect size (maximal distance between the two cumulative distributions, from 0 for identical distributions to 1 for fully separated ones). P-values were not used, as they are systematically significant with several thousand cells per sample.

```{r}
# Compute the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic for each QC metric
ks_stats <- sapply(metric_cols, function(m) {
  suppressWarnings(unname(ks.test(qc_metrics[[m]][qc_metrics$sample == "Manual"],
                                  qc_metrics[[m]][qc_metrics$sample == "Octo"])$statistic))
})

round(ks_stats, 3)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 5

# Define a violin plot function for one QC metric
qc_violin <- function(metric, ylab, log_y = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(qc_metrics, aes(x = sample, y = .data[[metric]], fill = sample)) +
    geom_violin(scale = "width") +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  if (log_y) p <- p + scale_y_log10()
  p
}

# Compare the distributions of the three QC metrics
qc_violin("nFeature_RNA", "Detected genes") +
  qc_violin("nCount_RNA", "UMIs (log scale)", log_y = TRUE) +
  qc_violin("percent_mt", "Mitochondrial transcripts (%)")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 4.5

# Define a cumulative-distribution plot function for one QC metric
qc_ecdf <- function(metric, xlab, log_x = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(qc_metrics, aes(x = .data[[metric]], colour = sample)) +
    stat_ecdf(linewidth = 0.8) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "Cumulative fraction of cells", colour = "Sample") +
    theme_classic()
  if (log_x) p <- p + scale_x_log10()
  p
}

# Compare the cumulative distributions of the three QC metrics
qc_ecdf("nFeature_RNA", "Detected genes") +
  qc_ecdf("nCount_RNA", "UMIs (log scale)", log_x = TRUE) +
  qc_ecdf("percent_mt", "Mitochondrial transcripts (%)") +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

The number of cells retained at each step and the ambient RNA correction were compared between the two samples. These summaries are read from the objects themselves, where each QC document stores them.

```{r}
# Build the QC funnel of the Octo sample
funnel_steps <- c("Candidate barcodes (at least 200 genes, after ambient correction)",
                  "After gene and UMI filters",
                  "After mitochondrial filter",
                  "After doublet removal (final)")
octo_funnel <- c(candidates = n_initial_cells, after_complexity = n_after_complexity,
                 after_mito = n_after_mito, final = n_final_cells)

# Compare the funnels when the Manual summary is available
if (is.null(manual_funnel)) {
  message("The Manual object carries no QC summary: re-render the Manual QC document.")
  funnel_comparison <- data.frame(step = funnel_steps[4], Manual = n_manual_final,
                                  Octo = n_final_cells)
} else {
  funnel_comparison <- data.frame(
    step = funnel_steps,
    Manual = unname(manual_funnel[names(octo_funnel)]),
    Octo = unname(octo_funnel)
  )
}
funnel_comparison
```

```{r}
# Compare the doublet rate and the fraction of Cell Ranger cells retained
if (!is.null(manual_funnel)) {
  funnel_extra <- data.frame(
    metric = c("Predicted doublets (% of cells after the mitochondrial filter)",
               "Final cells (% of Cell Ranger cells)"),
    Manual = round(c(100 * (1 - manual_funnel[["final"]] / manual_funnel[["after_mito"]]),
                     100 * manual_funnel[["final"]] / cellranger_cells[["Manual"]]), 1),
    Octo = round(c(100 * (1 - octo_funnel[["final"]] / octo_funnel[["after_mito"]]),
                   100 * octo_funnel[["final"]] / cellranger_cells[["Octo"]]), 1)
  )
  funnel_extra
}
```

```{r}
# Compare the ambient RNA correction of the two samples
if (!is.null(manual_soupx)) {
  ambient_comparison <- data.frame(
    metric = c("Estimated contamination fraction (rho)",
               "UMIs removed (% of the UMIs of the candidate cells)"),
    Manual = c(round(manual_soupx$rho, 3), manual_soupx$pct_removed),
    Octo = c(round(soupx_rho, 3), soupx_pct_removed)
  )
  ambient_comparison

  # Display the genes most affected by the correction in each sample
  cat("Manual:", paste(manual_soupx$top_genes, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  cat("Octo:  ", paste(names(top_soup_genes), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

The Octo sample retained `r fmt(n_final_cells)` cells and the Manual sample `r fmt(n_manual_final)` cells. The median number of detected genes was `r fmt(qc_summary_by_sample$median_genes[qc_summary_by_sample$sample == "Octo"])` for the Octo sample and `r fmt(qc_summary_by_sample$median_genes[qc_summary_by_sample$sample == "Manual"])` for the Manual sample, and the median number of UMIs was `r fmt(qc_summary_by_sample$median_umi[qc_summary_by_sample$sample == "Octo"])` and `r fmt(qc_summary_by_sample$median_umi[qc_summary_by_sample$sample == "Manual"])`, respectively. The Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics were `r round(ks_stats[["nFeature_RNA"]], 2)` for detected genes, `r round(ks_stats[["nCount_RNA"]], 2)` for UMIs and `r round(ks_stats[["percent_mt"]], 2)` for the mitochondrial percentage.

## Normalisation

The retained count matrix was normalised using Seurat's `LogNormalize` method, as for the Manual sample. For each cell, gene counts were divided by the total cellular count, multiplied by the default scale factor of 10,000 and log-transformed. `SCTransform` is a possible alternative, but it requires more computational resources since it fits generalised linear models to adjust the residuals.

```{r}
# Normalise gene expression while preserving the raw counts
sobjFiltrd <- NormalizeData(
  object = sobjFiltrd,
  normalization.method = "LogNormalize",
  scale.factor = 10000,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

Raw counts remained available in the `counts` layer, while the normalised expression values were stored in the `data` layer.

```{r}
# Verify the RNA layers present after normalisation
Layers(sobjFiltrd[["RNA"]])
```

Sample labels were added to the cell metadata for the joint analysis of the two samples.

```{r}
# Add the sample and dissociation-method labels
sobjFiltrd$sample <- sample_label
sobjFiltrd$dissociation <- "gentleMACS Octo"

table(sobjFiltrd$sample)
```

## Saving the filtered object

The filtered and normalised Seurat object was saved for the integration analysis. It keeps the object name `sobjFiltrd` used for the Manual sample; the two objects are therefore loaded into separate environments in the integration document.

```{r}
# Store the QC summary with the object for the joint analysis
Misc(sobjFiltrd, slot = "qc_funnel") <- c(candidates = n_initial_cells,
                                         after_complexity = n_after_complexity,
                                         after_mito = n_after_mito,
                                         final = n_final_cells)
Misc(sobjFiltrd, slot = "soupx") <- list(rho = soupx_rho, pct_removed = soupx_pct_removed,
                                        top_genes = names(top_soup_genes))

# Define the output path
filtered_output_file <- paste0("../data/processed_data/", sample.name, "_FILTERED.rda")

# Save the filtered and normalised Seurat object
save(sobjFiltrd, file = filtered_output_file)

cat("Filtered object saved to:", filtered_output_file, "\n")
```
